chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who have faith.
But upon those who take him as their master.

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُمْ: Those who take him as master/ally

ai.seo_question: Who does Satan have authority over according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifying that Satan's authority (*sulṭān*) is not absolute over all believers but conditional upon their choice to ally with him, a nuance central to Shia theological debates on free will versus predestination. This distinction refutes the notion of compulsion (*jabr*), affirming that while Satan can influence, he cannot force a believer to lose faith unless they willingly submit to his guidance. The narration underscores the practical implication that spiritual vigilance (*muraqabah*) is required to prevent Satan from becoming one's *khalīl* (close friend/ally).
